name: InterContinental Edinburgh The George
insider_take: This Georgian masterpiece sits on George Street, one of Edinburgh's most prestigious addresses, where literary legends like Sir Walter Scott once walked these very sidewalks.
whats_special: Built in 1775, The George is part of Edinburgh's UNESCO World Heritage New Town. The hotel's original Assembly Rooms hosted Jane Austen-era balls, and Room 322 is rumored to be haunted by a Victorian-era guest who still occasionally rearranges furniture.
pro_tip: Request a room facing George Street for stunning views of the First New Town's perfectly preserved Georgian architecture—it's like staying inside a living museum.
dont_miss: The hotel's Printing Press Bar & Kitchen occupies the former site of Edinburgh's first printing press. Step outside to discover you're equidistant from Edinburgh Castle and the Royal Mile—making this the perfect base for exploring both Old and New Town on foot.
pros: Prime location on George Street in Edinburgh's city center
Historic Georgian architecture with modern luxury amenities
Exceptional service standards from InterContinental brand
Walking distance to Edinburgh Castle and Royal Mile attractions
cons: Premium pricing due to luxury positioning and prime location
Limited parking availability in busy city center location
